[1/2] Plan: normalize legacy landable flags on load from one shared surface-type set

impact_assessment.why: Existing saves persist landable=false for gas/lava worlds, so they cannot use the operations unlocked in Cycle 5; generation and migration also duplicated the landable policy.
impact_assessment.benefits: Legacy saves gain LAND ON SURFACE, Cloud Scoop and Magma Tap on load without rewriting ownership or population; one policy constant.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: galaxy imports surface (no cycle); concurrency: constructor migration under existing load path; state: only the persisted landable boolean changes.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Legacy 474KB save play, ownership/government assertions, before/after target-card captures.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan: pay the landing survey reward once per body and persist surveyed bodies

impact_assessment.why: land_on_body awards 150 + radius/1000*5 credits on every landing; a ringed giant pays +450 cr each time, so leave-and-reland farms credits indefinitely.
impact_assessment.benefits: Survey rewards become a real one-time discovery while repeat landings still open surface operations; old saves remain loadable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ShipState gains one additive tuple (old saves default empty); dependency: none; concurrency: engine lock held; state: surveyed set grows one id per body.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first engine test, save round-trip/default test, before/after scripted land-travel-land run, full suite.

[1/3] Plan: default the left console to five core tabs plus one MORE SYSTEMS disclosure

impact_assessment.why: The terminal exposes 16 first-level tabs simultaneously; the core loop (player, ship, commerce, fleet, contracts) is buried among advanced systems, and the rail competes with the radar and command strip.
impact_assessment.benefits: The default rail drops from 16 tabs to 6 visible choices, keeps every advanced mechanic one click away, and lets keyboard cycling reveal advanced tabs automatically.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: static UI surface, new control; dependency: none; concurrency: tab rendering stays synchronous; state: purely in-memory advanced-visible flag, no save field; navigation tests and click-map counts may change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Static focus-rail test, before/after visible-count and click-through play, vision review, UI snapshot and full gates.

[1/2] Plan: remove the duplicated PLAYER ability set and point to the command strip

impact_assessment.why: PLAYER renders six ability cards with USE buttons while the bottom command strip already exposes the same six with hotkeys and cooldowns; G-013 forbids the duplicate.
impact_assessment.benefits: PLAYER content height roughly halves, duplicate controls disappear, and one ability surface remains authoritative.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: G-013-aligned UI; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; regression: bottom strip must keep firing.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Static dedup test, before/after control counts, bottom-strip Overclock play, vision review.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan: collapse the SHIP room schematic and module catalog behind SHOW controls

impact_assessment.why: SHIP is the largest core tab at 2,390px; the six-room schematic and 12-row catalog are always open, overflow horizontally at 1280, and bury the ship/stat overview.
impact_assessment.benefits: Initial SHIP content drops below 1,000px while all rooms and modules remain one click away with clear HIDE controls.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI surface; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: in-memory hidden attributes only; regression: open panel must show all rooms and module rows.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Static disclosure test, before/after height and horizontal-width measurements, open-state play, vision review.

[1/2] Plan: keep the COMMERCE exchange first and collapse auto-trade plus quantum freight below it

impact_assessment.why: COMMERCE is the next densest core tab at 2076px; the auto-trade broker and quantum freight sit between the services row and the market, so the exchange and its price rows never reach the first screen at 1280x720.
impact_assessment.benefits: The market table becomes the primary surface, the broker and freight stay one click away, and dense service/filter/market rows stop overflowing at 1280.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI surface; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: hidden attributes and existing trade state only, no save change; regression: the exchange, services and both disclosures must stay reachable.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Static disclosure/order tests, before/after height and width measurements, open-state browser play, vision review, UI snapshot and full gates.
